Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray shows a markedly smaller and hyperlucent right hemithorax with diminished vascular markings, indicative of oligemia. Combined with the patient's history of Takayasu arteritis and the CT finding of calcification/occlusion in the pulmonary artery (arrow), this appearance is classic for chronic obstruction of the right pulmonary artery leading to hypoplasia or atrophy of the lung.
